data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The team should adopt an existing experiment tracker but enforce a 'Control-Plane Separation' mechanism: the external tool serves strictly as a passive, append-only log store (the 'Data Plane'), while all logic governing experiment flow, active learning loops, and state transitions resides in a local, version-controlled orchestrator script (the 'Control Plane') that pushes finalized metrics to the tracker via its API.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The existing tool lacks an append-only API or forces interactive UI workflows that cannot be bypassed programmatically.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The latency introduced by the local orchestrator pushing to the remote tracker disrupts time-sensitive active learning feedback loops.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain the local orchestrator's state machine correctness over time.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Control-Plane Separation decouples the causal agency of the research loop from the storage infrastructure. By retaining the state machine locally, the team preserves the ability to implement novel active learning strategies without fighting the rigid workflow assumptions of off-the-shelf tools (addressing the 'integration tax'). Simultaneously, by forcing all data through the external tool's API only after local validation against a strict schema, the approach prevents the 'migration cliff' of unstructured noise and ensures the external tool remains a reliable, queryable archive rather than a fragile single point of failure for the team's cognitive model.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
